title: Water + ethanol + cyclohexane, NRTL, 20 stages and a decanter: heterogeneous azeotropic distillation with an entrainer
purpose: Proposal 0024's validated case (the maintainer, 2026-11-14): heterogeneous azeotropic distillation with an entrainer and a decanter on the condenser. The cyclohexane-rich (light) liquid of the decanter is refluxed, the water-rich one is the distillate. At this bottoms flow the stages below the feed hold two liquids and their vapour is the model's ternary heterogeneous azeotrope, which is compared with the measured one of Gomis et al. (2005), validation/data/lle/water_ethanol_cyclohexane_vlle_gomis2005.json. Not a design: the feed carries its own entrainer, and the bottoms are not dry ethanol.
method_choice: docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md rules 3 and 7: polar, below 10 bar, two liquids: NRTL with the default sets, each fitted to open measured data (ethanol + water fitted-kamihama2012; water + cyclohexane fitted-marche2006-etal, mutual solubilities; ethanol + cyclohexane fitted-reddy2013; src/data/binaries.json), ideal-gas vapour. None was fitted to ternary data.

behaviour: two liquids on the stages the reference names (fixture columns-vll-three-phase.json, each stage's `liquids`)
the vapour of the two-liquid stages is the model's ternary heterogeneous azeotrope: a liquid of that composition boils at that temperature (the three-phase flash) and gives that vapour
the decanter's two liquids lie on the model's tie line at the decanter's temperature
expected.branch: The engine's solution from its own start; the reference (validation/python/reference_mesh_vll.py, ChemSep's three-phase stage) solves its own equations from the engine's profile, perturbed.

engine_against_reference.why: Proposal 0015, Engineering basis: flows within 1e-6 relative of the independent MESH solution. Both solve the same equations to residuals of 1e-8 or less, so the difference is the solvers' convergence only.

balances_on_every_stage.why: Proposal 0015: every stage's balances closed to 1e-8. Material: |residual| / F; energy: |residual| / (F x 10 kJ/mol); summation and equilibrium are mole fractions.

stability.why: one-liquid stages: no trial liquid on a grid has a tangent-plane distance below -1e-9

agreement_with_data.note: The three NRTL sets are fitted to vapour-liquid data; their liquid-liquid split is W1's work (joint fits, M2b) and not a test of the column.
